answer: Bonded identity-uniqueness challenge resists sybils: to register, an identity stakes a bond AND answers a periodic proof that it is distinct from existing members (e.g. a non-collision proof against a registry), with the bond slashed if a duplicate is later proven. An onyx-hard deposit backs every claim of distinctness; a prism of fakes each risks its stake on a lie that later evidence can shatter. Honest unique agents keep their bonds; a swarm claiming many distinct identities from one operator forfeits basalt-heavy collateral when the duplication surfaces.
